keyVerseText: And when he was in the gate of Benjamin, a captain of the ward was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he took Jeremiah the prophet, saying, Thou fallest away to the Chaldeans.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun פְּקִדֻת (pᵉqiduth) derives from the root פָּקִיד (pâqîyd), which refers to one who has charge or oversight, such as a governor or overseer. This root conveys the idea of a designated official entrusted with responsibility and supervision, whether civil, military, or religious. Thus, פְּקִדֻת carries the literal sense of a ward or a charge under watchful care, emphasizing active oversight rather than passive possession.
usageInScripture: The term פְּקִדֻת appears only once in the Hebrew Scriptures, where it is translated as "of the ward" in Jeremiah 37:13. This singular occurrence highlights its specific application to a position of guardianship or sentry duty, underscoring the role of an appointed overseer responsible for security and vigilance. The consistency in translation reflects its narrow semantic range focused on supervision and guarding.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding פְּקִדֻת as an appointed ward or oversight enriches our grasp of God’s providential governance. Just as a human overseer is entrusted with responsibility and vigilance, God’s sovereign oversight extends over His people with care and authority. This word reminds believers of the divine order in which leadership and accountability serve to protect and guide, reflecting the faithful stewardship God exercises over His covenant community. It also points to the importance of faithful watchfulness and obedience within the body of Christ, modeled on God’s own supervisory care.
keyVerseReflection: In Jeremiah 37:13, the phrase "a captain of the ward" (פְּקִדֻת) identifies a military overseer stationed at the gate, responsible for security and order. The use of this term emphasizes the official's role in guarding and supervising, which in this context leads to the apprehension of the prophet Jeremiah. This highlights the practical function of פְּקִדֻת as one who exercises authority and vigilance, illustrating the intersection of spiritual and civil oversight in the biblical narrative.
